records.central_bank: National Bank of the Republic of Belarus
records.people: Deputy Head of Department, National Bank of the Republic of Belarus (1998-2005), afterwards in senior roles at Priorbank (2005-2016)
records.move: from Deputy Head of Department at the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus (1998-2005) to Priorbank (Raiffeisen Group), 2005-2016, in roles including Head of the Project Management Office, Chief Digital Officer and Head of Retail Banking
records.summary: A career page published by Ipoteka Bank sets out an unbroken record: 1998 to 2005 at the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus, finishing as Deputy Head of Department, then 2005 to 2016 at Priorbank, listed on that page as part of the Raiffeisen Group, in roles including Head of the Project Management Office, Chief Digital Officer and Head of Retail Banking, then 2016 to 2023 at Dabrabyt Bank. Who owns Priorbank is stated by a separate report on the bank's sale, which calls Priorbank 'the largest private bank in Belarus' and says that '87.74% of shares in Priorbank OJSC will be transferred to SOVEN 1', the 87.74% stake having been held until then through a subsidiary of the Austrian group Raiffeisen Bank International AG. The central bank role here was below senior management, so the role is given and the name is not.
records.source_title: Bank management information: Deputy Chairman of the Management Board (Ipoteka Bank)
records.ownership_quote: the largest private bank in Belarus

records.people: Farhat Bengdara (Deputy Governor, then Governor of the Central Bank of Libya, 2006-2011)
records.move: from Governor of the Central Bank of Libya (2006-2011) to the board of directors of UniCredit SpA as board member and vice-chairman, from 29 April 2009
records.summary: Farhat Bengdara was Deputy Governor and then Governor of the Central Bank of Libya from 2006 to 2011, and from 29 April 2009 he sat on the board of UniCredit SpA as board member and vice-chairman, so the two roles overlapped. UniCredit's own shareholder-structure page sets out who holds the shares: Aabar Luxembourg S.A.R.L. 5.039%, BlackRock Inc. 4.993% in non-discretional asset management, Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio Verona, Vicenza, Belluno e Ancona 3.460%, Central Bank of Libya 2.923% and Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Torino 2.517%. That table is mixed: most of the named holders are private investors and foundations, and one, the Central Bank of Libya itself, is a state body. The career list comes from a Wikipedia article, so the source is marked weak.

held.why_held: Three career lists read in full and none names a private employer: the Central Bank of Iraq's own CV page for the acting Deputy Governor (university lecturing then four CBI departments), the CBI's history page (governor tenures only, no other employers), the new governor Nazar Nasser Hussein (25 years at the CBI, then the Iraqi Office for Anti-Money Laundering), and Deputy Governor Faisal Wisam al-Heims (Trade Bank of Iraq, described in the article as a state-owned bank, and the Iraq Securities Commission). No ownership statement needed because no private-looking employer appeared.

Two Bhutanese career lists found, both ending in public bodies. Dasho Penjore: Royal Monetary Authority from 1987, Deputy Managing Director 2003-2006, Chief Chamberlain from 2006, CEO of the National Pension & Provident Fund, Governor from December 2015 - the pension fund is a statutory body. Damche Tenzin: High Court, Royal Civil Service Commission 1997-2008, Bank of Bhutan Limited 2008-2014 as Chief Legal Advisor and Company Secretary, National Pension & Provident Fund 2015-2016, then RMA Chief General Counsel from June 2016. No source read states who owns Bank of Bhutan Limited. Bhutan National Bank's 2022 annual report was read to character 200,000 of 335,600 and gives only total share capital of Nu 3,950,323,110 with no holder breakdown and no director biographies.

The Wikipedia biography of Governor Oscar Humberto Evora Santos names only the Bank of Cape Verde, Praia city council (mayor 2016-2020), the World Bank in 1994 and the United Nations in 2000 - no commercial bank at all. The official act surfaced for Banco de Cabo Verde board appointments turned out to be Lei n.o 70/X/2026, the bank's new organic law, which names nobody except the two signatories. No career list naming a private employer was found, so there was nothing to check ownership on.

Three career lists read and none names a private bank. Governor Aivo Andrianarivelo: head of a privatisation/training fund 2008-2020 and IMF Executive Director from February 2020. Henri Rabarijohn's resignation report gives no employer other than the central bank. The Central Banking report on Vonimanitra Razafimbelo's promotion names only her central bank roles and is partly behind a subscription barrier. The BNI Madagascar appointment of Patrice Mazzei names Natixis Algerie but makes no mention of the Banque Centrale de Madagascar and says nothing about BNI's shareholders. The bank's own sites banky-foibe.mg and bfm.mg were not retried in this round.

Two private-bank documents were read for a central bank career and neither gives one. Banco Lopez de Haro's 2023 corporate governance report lists nine shareholders above 3%, all named individuals, companies and a trust with percentages, but gives no previous employer for any of its ten directors. Grupo Popular's 2023 list of principal executives of Banco Popular Dominicano gives names and current titles only, with no career histories and no ownership statement. A report on BHD's 2025 executive changes gives long internal careers at Banco BHD and no Banco Central role and no ownership statement. Governor Hector Valdez Albizu's own career is reported as 50 years inside the Banco Central.

No career list for a Banco Central de Cuba official was opened within budget; searching surfaced only appointment and dismissal reports and a Wikipedia institutional article, none of which carries a career list with a private employer. No source states that any Cuban bank an official worked for is privately owned.

searched_no_result: Central Bank of Iraq, cbi.iq/page/52, the CV section for the acting Deputy Governor (Dr Ammar Hamad Khalaf Ibrahim): five numbered posts read, University of Baghdad 2010-2017 then four CBI departments 2017 to present; no private employer. The phrases 'Gulf Commercial Bank' and 'private Iraqi banks' appear only in the titles of his research papers.

Central Bank of Iraq, cbi.iq/page/49, the history page's ex-governors list: names and governorship dates only, from Ali Nour al-Din al-Anezi (1955-1961) to Ali Mohsen Al-Allaq (to 21 June 2026); no other employer for anyone.

The National (thenationalnews.com, 22 June 2026), the biography paragraphs on new CBI governor Nazar Nasser Hussein: 25 years of legal, administrative and supervisory roles at the CBI and director general of the Iraqi Office for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing. No private employer.

Shafaq News, 'CBI governor appoints a seasoned banker as his deputy', the career paragraphs on Faisal Wisam al-Heims: Director-General of the Trade Bank of Iraq, which the article itself calls a state-owned bank, and Chairman of the Iraq Securities Commission.
Central Bank of Libya, cbl.gov.ly/en/?p=865, the History page and its ex-governors table: names and dates only, to Saddek Omar ElKaber (2011-2024); no career details for anyone.

Wikipedia, 'Oscar Humberto Evora Santos', the whole biography: Bank of Cape Verde governor from 4 January 2021, Praia mayor 2016-2020, World Bank 1994, United Nations 2000. No commercial or private bank named.

Boletim Oficial de Cabo Verde, act id=89469: this is Lei n.o 70/X/2026, the new organic law of the Banco de Cabo Verde of 26 January 2026. Article 3 is a transitional clause keeping the sitting Governor and Administration Board in office but naming nobody.

capmad.com, 'Aivo Andrianarivelo Assumes Governorship at the Central Bank of Madagascar', the career paragraph: head of the privatisation/training fund 2008-2020 and IMF Executive Director from February 2020; the article says he 'held various significant roles within the financial sector' but names no firm.
L'Express de Madagascar, 5 January 2023, 'Hautes finances: Henri Rabarijohn quitte le gouvernail de la Banque centrale', the whole item: his governorship and departure only, no other employer named.

Central Banking, 'Madagascan deputy steps up to top job' (node/2301385), the visible biography of Vonimanitra Razafimbelo: deputy director-general made interim governor, retaining the directorship of the bank's general administration; no previous employer. Text cuts off at a subscription barrier.

L'Express de Madagascar, September 2025, 'BNI Madagascar - Patrice Mazzei nomme directeur general par interim', the career paragraph: BNI Madagascar Risk Director then interim Managing Director from 1 October 2025, previously Risk and Compliance Director at Natixis Algerie. No Banque Centrale de Madagascar role; no shareholder information for BNI.

FITI (fiti.bt) staff page for Dasho Penjore, the whole biography: Royal Monetary Authority from 1987 and Deputy Managing Director 2003-2006, Chief Chamberlain from 2006, CEO of the National Pension & Provident Fund, Governor from December 2015, FITI board chairperson. No bank named.

FITI (fiti.bt) board PDF for Damche Tenzin, the full employment-history table: High Court 1995-1996, Royal Civil Service Commission 1997-2008, Bank of Bhutan Limited 2008-2014, National Pension & Provident Fund 2015-2016, Royal Monetary Authority Chief General Counsel from June 2016. The page does not state who owns Bank of Bhutan Limited.

Bhutan National Bank Annual Report 2022, read to character 200,000 of 335,600 including the financial-statement notes: Note 32 gives total share capital of Nu 3,950,323,110 with no holder breakdown; Note 26 covers subordinated bonds including certificates issued to RGoB, not shares. The board and management pages give names and roles only, with no employment histories.
Bhutan National Bank, notice to shareholders of 30 March 2026: a board-nomination procedure only. No shareholder names, no percentages, no director biographies.

Banco Lopez de Haro, Informe Anual de Gobierno Corporativo 2023, the significant-shareholders table and the board-composition section: nine holders above 3% named with percentages (all individuals, companies and a trust, 67 shareholders in total) but no previous employer for any of the ten directors, so no Banco Central career to pair with it.
Grupo Popular, IGA 2023 'Principales Ejecutivos Banco Popular Dominicano' PDF, the full executive list: fifteen names with current titles only, no career histories, no ownership statement.

Revista Mercado, 'BHD refuerza su gobierno corporativo con cambios en su cupula ejecutiva', the biography paragraphs for Andres Maldonado, Fidelio Arturo Despradel, Vera Jean Jimenez and Luis Lembert: long internal careers at Banco BHD and Grupo BHD, no Banco Central role, no ownership statement.
RBI, Raiffeisen Belarus network page: no named chief executive or management board, but states RBI held 87.7% of the shares as of December 2023, with 12.3% held by others.
